17.0.0.en: This chapter and the next tell the story of Micah's image, which reveals the extent of the spiritual blindness into which the people, and likewise the Levites, had fallen, a blindness shown in idolatrous worship mixed with a mere outward form of worshipping God. This story happened during the period of the judges. It tells of a man named Micah, who lived in the hill country that belonged to the tribe of Ephraim, and who had stolen from his mother a sum of money, eleven hundred shekels of silver (v. 2).

17.1.0.en: A shekel of silver: equal to about 11-15 grams of silver.

17.1.1.en: I cursed and also spoke in my ears: You cursed, O mother, and I heard the curse with my ears.

17.1.2.en: When his mother discovered the theft and did not know who the thief was, she began to curse the thief. The son could not bear to hear the curse with his ears, and he feared that his mother's curse would fall upon him, so he confessed to her that he was the one who had stolen the silver and that it was in his possession. The mother commended her son's confession and blessed him in place of the curse she had pronounced before.

17.2.0.en: Micah returned to his mother the silver he had stolen. She refused to put it back in her treasury, but vowed to dedicate it to the Lord by making a graven image, that is, one shaped with carving tools, and another made by melting metal and pouring it into a mold in the form of an image, and Micah would place them in his house to worship them. She gave the silver to her son Micah to make the images.

17.3.0.en: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she set aside two hundred shekels of it to make the two images and gave it to the craftsman, who made the two required images, one graven and the other molten, and Micah placed them in his house. The mother gave the rest of the sum to her son to spend on the service and worship of the two images.

17.4.0.en: Ephod: a linen garment worn by the priest.

17.4.1.en: Teraphim: small images that people kept in their houses for worship and to bring good fortune.

17.4.2.en: He consecrated one of his sons: he appointed one of his sons and set him apart for the service.

17.4.3.en: Micah had set apart a place in his house for worship. He placed the two images in it, made an ephod, and consecrated one of his sons to be a priest for the family, performing the priestly service.

17.4.4.en: What Micah did, many do today, choosing gods for themselves, such as money or honor, and choosing priests after their own desires, to tell them what suits their desires and not the voice of God.

17.5.0.en: This story reveals the depth of ignorance to which that family had sunk, and it was not an isolated case but an example of the general corruption that prevailed among the people. Among the many errors that this story reveals, into which Micah and his mother fell, was setting up a private shrine in his house, although the one house in which worship was to be offered to the Lord was the house of God in "Shiloh." Micah also made for himself two images and teraphim, which the Law utterly forbade; and he set up his son as a priest, though he was not of the seed of Aaron. This verse fixes the time of what Micah did: it was the age of the judges, before kings were set up over the children of Israel. In this period the people of God sometimes held fast to God's commandments and to His Law given by Moses, as the judges taught it, and at other times they drifted away from it, and the enemies around them humbled them. This is one picture of spiritual ignorance.

17.5.1.en: All these errors that Micah and his mother committed teach us that a people without a teacher to guide them are exposed to spiritual dangers and perhaps even to eternal spiritual perdition, for the Scripture says, "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge" (Hos 4:6). Therefore let us pray to God to preserve the shepherds of our Church, that they may "rightly divide for us the word of truth," and let us submit to their teachings and guidance so that we do not go astray.

17.6.0.en: Bethlehem-judah: it lies nine kilometers south of Jerusalem, and it is the place where Christ was born (Map 10). There was a young man living in Bethlehem in the land of Judah. Though he is said to be of the family of Judah, in truth he was of the tribe of the Levites, of the family of the Gershomites, as is stated in (ch. 18:30), but he was living among the family of Judah. The Levites had cities in which they lived among the tribes. (Ch. 18:30) mentions that the name of this Levite was Jonathan.

17.7.0.en: Where he could find a place: to any place, seeking a livelihood.

17.7.1.en: He came on his way: going on his way.

17.7.2.en: Poverty drove this young man to leave Bethlehem for another place in search of a livelihood. He came to the hill country of Ephraim, and on his way he chanced upon Micah's house and turned aside to it to ask about work. In this the Levite abandoned his work as a teacher of the people and a servant of the house of God and began to seek money and honor. This is a picture of the decline of the Levites in the age of the judges.

17.8.0.en: Micah asked him where he was from, and he answered that he was from the tribe of Levi, that he had been living in Bethlehem before coming here, and that he had decided to leave his town and go seeking a livelihood in any other place where he might settle.

17.9.0.en: Micah rejoiced in the young Levite and asked him to stay with him to be a priest to him in place of his son, thinking that by this he would complete the ideal picture of worship: he had the ephod and the teraphim, and here was a true priest from the tribe of Levi to lead the worship in his house, which would be better than his son. He offered him a yearly wage in addition to his clothing and his food, and called him father, that is, one responsible for Micah and his family in praying for them. The Levite found this offer a generous one for him compared with the circumstances in which he had lived before, so he agreed to Micah's offer.

17.10.0.en: The Levite accepted to stay with Micah, and Micah treated him very well, loving him and honoring him. While the Levite was in effect a spiritual father with regard to the priesthood, Micah treated him as one of his sons.

17.11.0.en: Micah consecrated the Levite as his priest and gave him all his rights as a priest. So the Levite settled permanently in his house with Micah's family and served in the house that Micah had earlier set apart for worship (v. 5).

17.12.0.en: Micah was very glad of the Levite, for he knew that the Law prescribes that this tribe is the one set apart for the priesthood, although the priesthood was confined to the seed of Aaron. Yet he saw that the Levite, in any case, belongs to this holy tribe for the service of God and was more entitled than his son to do this spiritual work, believing that it was God who had brought this Levite across his path, and that by this He wished to do him good and bless him. This shows the extent of the spiritual ignorance that prevailed at that time.

17.12.1.en: Honoring the priests and servants who labor faithfully in the service of God gladdens the heart of God, but with wisdom in this honor toward those you know, so that you encourage them and help them to care for all souls and to complete their service. The tribe of Dan seeks a land to possess

18.0.s.en: (1) The tribe of Dan chooses Laish to possess it

18.0.0.en: The book fixes the time of the events mentioned in this chapter as the age of the judges, that is, before the age of the kings began among the people of God. It makes clear that the portion of the tribe of Dan that it received in the Promised Land was small and lay beside the Mediterranean Sea, west of the tribes of Benjamin and Judah and the western half of the tribe of Manasseh. It appears that the Amorites, the pagan inhabitants of the land, harassed the tribe of Dan and settled beside them in the fertile valleys, so the tribe of Dan was forced to live in the mountains and so did not have a sufficient portion among the tribes. Their zeal and concern appeared in seeking another land to possess that would be wide enough for their growing numbers.

18.1.0.en: As is customary in wars, the tribe of Dan sent a group of strong men from two famous cities in the land of Dan, Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land in order to find a suitable place that the tribe would fight to obtain. In the course of their travels these men came down into the land of the tribe of Ephraim and lodged at the estate that belonged to Micah, which was a place prepared for receiving strangers to stay in.

18.2.0.en: While they were at Micah's house, they heard the voice of the Levite as he was serving in the shrine belonging to Micah's family, and they recognized him because they had seen him before, since he had lived in Bethlehem, which lies in the portion of the tribe of Judah, and there was close association between the tribes of Judah and Dan. So they went toward the place of the voice and asked him what had brought him here and what he was doing in this place.

18.3.0.en: The young man told them what had happened to him: how he had left his town, how Micah had welcomed him, what he had offered him of staying with him, and how he served as a priest for the family in return for a fixed wage, food, and clothing.

18.4.0.en: When the spies of the tribe of Dan learned that the Levite served in the office of priesthood, they asked him to inquire of the Lord concerning what they had resolved to do. Thus the spiritual ignorance of the people of God appears, for they thought that this Levite was able to do what the high priests used to do by means of the Urim and Thummim in the tabernacle of meeting, while this Levite was performing the rites of the worship of idols, the teraphim, and the false gods, which cannot foretell anything to anyone through him. This also shows the extent of the confusion that prevailed in that time and the mixing of the worship of God with the worship of idols.

18.4.1.en: Therefore God sets up in His Church bishops and elders who govern, to shepherd the people faithfully and to preserve the doctrine without any confusion, and "as they once received it from the saints." The Church has always preserved the ancient faith from the distortion of heretics and those who depart from the faith, so they have been and remain guardians of the right doctrine and the appointed rites, as is prayed in the Litany of the Archpriests and Priests in the Divine Liturgy: "And those who rightly divide with him the word of truth, grant them to Your holy Church, that they may shepherd Your flock in peace."

18.5.0.en: The Levite (the priest) pretended that God was inspiring him, and he told them what they believed to be divine counsel, and prophesied to them that they would be under God's care wherever they went.

18.6.0.en: The Sidonians: the inhabitants of Sidon, which lies on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, south of the city of Tyre.

18.6.1.en: There was no magistrate in the land, that might put them to shame in any thing, as an heir of authority: no one to harm them in anything, and no ruler who had inherited rule from those before him lorded it over them.

18.6.2.en: They had no business with any man: they had no quarrel with anyone, nor any alliances with others.

18.6.3.en: The five men walked through the land of Canaan until they reached a city in the far northeast near Mount Hermon, the city of Laish. Its inhabitants were Sidonians who had migrated from their original city, and like all Sidonians they were fond of maritime occupations, fishing and trade. They had settled there content with their life and their work, with no enmities or alliances with anyone outside, and no one tyrannized over them from within. They were without a king and completely independent of those around them, even of Sidon, because of the distance between Sidon and Laish, for the first lies in the far northwest and the second in the far northeast.

18.7.0.en: The five men returned from their scouting journey to their city in Zorah and Eshtaol, and the people of their tribe asked them what they had found on this journey and what was the news of the lands and their inhabitants.

18.8.0.en: The five spies advised the men of their tribe not to delay or be slothful, but to go up at once to "Laish" to possess it, for the land was very good and all the circumstances were favorable for taking it.

18.9.0.en: The five men went on recounting the facts they had learned about the land they had spied out. They told their brethren that if they came to Laish they would find a people not expecting anyone to attack them, who made no preparations or fortifications to defend their city. They also told them that the land was wide and far-stretching, that is, able to hold all the sons of their tribe, besides the richness of the land and the abundance of its goods, so that whoever lived in it would need nothing from outside. They also assured them that God would give them the land according to His promise to His people through Moses and Joshua.

18.9.1.en: The tribe of Dan took courage to carry out God's commands to drive out the pagan inhabitants of the land. So do not hesitate to carry out God's commandments, and you will find your rest and your fullness, and trust in the power of God that supports you, and you will defeat all your enemies, the demons.

18.10.s.en: (2) The theft of Micah's priest and images

18.10.0.en: The men of the tribe were persuaded by what their five messengers told them and decided to invade the city of Laish. So they equipped six hundred warriors from among them, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, supplied them with weapons and fighting equipment, and set out toward Laish.

18.11.0.en: The town of Kirjath-jearim: it lies on the border of Judah and Dan near the city of Zorah, 14.5 km west of Jerusalem. It is one of the four cities of the Gibeonites (Josh 9:17). Behind Kirjath-jearim: west of the town of Kirjath-jearim.

18.11.1.en: The men of war set out from their cities, Zorah and Eshtaol, and reached one of the cities of Judah near Zorah and stayed some time in that place. Therefore it was called "Mahaneh-dan," and it kept this name until the time this book was written.

18.12.0.en: From there they went north to the hill country of Ephraim until they reached the place where Micah lived.

18.13.0.en: The five spies, who had already seen the region, told them that there was an ephod, teraphim, a graven image, and a molten image in Micah's house, and they encouraged their brethren not to neglect these precious things but to work to take them to be a blessing for their tribe, as they believed. This confirms the spiritual error in which the people of God lived in this period, since they counted the images of idols as something great.

18.14.0.en: The soldiers responded to the call of the five men and decided to seize those things. So they went to the place where they were kept, which was the shrine that Micah had set apart for that purpose. The young Levite was performing the religious rites when they came, and when they arrived they spoke with him.

18.15.0.en: Their conversation with the Levite took place at the door of the house, where the six hundred warriors of the children of Dan stood armed with weapons of war.

18.16.0.en: The priest was startled to find six hundred armed men and was very afraid. Meanwhile the five spies went in and took the two images, the ephod, and the teraphim from the shrine.

18.17.0.en: The priest was astonished at their stealing the images and tried to object to the five men.

18.18.0.en: The men rebuked him and commanded him to be silent and not to open his mouth in any objection or to argue with them about what they had done. Rather, they asked him to go with them to be priest to them and to be a spiritual father to their tribe, for in this he would be priest to a great company, a whole tribe of the tribes of Israel, and this was better for him than being priest to one family. Thus they used violence and rebuke with him, and also enticement: they threatened him with the armed men and at the same time enticed him to become a priest and spiritual father to a whole tribe.

18.19.0.en: The priest's heart was glad: he rejoiced and was delighted.

18.19.1.en: He went in the midst of the people: he walked among them.

18.19.2.en: This was a tempting offer for the Levite, for the soldiers of the tribe of Dan succeeded in bringing a spirit of boasting and pride into his heart; no doubt his moral standing would rise by being priest to a tribe instead of priest to a family, and besides, he expected his wage and his share of the offerings of a whole tribe to increase. So he overlooked their taking the ephod, the teraphim, and the images, and walked in the midst of the soldiers, declaring by this his agreement to the offer made to him by the tribe.

18.19.3.en: The men of Dan made theft lawful for themselves, and they stole what leads astray from God, namely the idols. Do not break the commandment and become occupied with the possessions of the world. They are all vanity, and do not clash with others because of them, but rather possess God in your heart, and He will bless your life, and you will lack nothing.

18.20.s.en: (3) Micah tries to recover his property

18.20.0.en: They put the carriage before them: they put their baggage in front of them.

18.20.1.en: The soldiers left Micah's house, heading for Laish, and they placed their little ones, their women, their cattle, and their baggage in front, and the men walked behind them to guard them and protect them from any attack that an enemy might make on them.

18.21.0.en: Some time passed until Micah noticed the Levite's absence and discovered the theft of his sacred things. He gathered his relatives and those working in his house to pursue the men of the tribe of Dan, hoping to recover what they had taken from him, until they overtook them.

18.22.0.en: Micah and his men cried out, calling the men of the tribe of Dan to pay attention to him and hear his protest. They turned to him in disapproval, asking him scornfully what this crying out was and who these men were that he had brought, and what had happened that he should do all this.

18.23.0.en: What have I more?: what is left to me after what you have taken from me.

18.23.1.en: Micah answered them, protesting at what they had done in taking the idols and the teraphim and also his Levite priest, for by this they had deprived him of the most precious thing he owned, leaving him nothing. And after doing all this, they objected to his crying out and protesting.

18.24.0.en: Let not thy voice be heard among us: do not speak.

18.24.1.en: Angry fellows: in great distress and ready to strike down whoever opposes them.

18.24.2.en: The Danite soldiers threatened him that if he did not be silent and stop crying out, they would not bear with him any longer, for they were weary and troubled by the length of the journey and by their thinking about the hard task, the task of the war they were about to undertake, and if he persisted in his crying out and in following them on their march, they would kill him and all who were with him.

18.25.0.en: The men of Dan disregarded Micah's words and continued on their way toward Laish, and Micah felt that there was no use in protesting and even feared them, so he returned to his house.

18.25.1.en: Do not become involved in evil, like Micah who made idols, lest you lose much, and if you lose, take heed to return to God by repentance and keep away from evil, and do not do as Micah did, who returned to his house but did not understand God's message to turn away from the worship of idols.

18.26.0.en: The Danites reached the city of Laish, with the two images, the ephod, and the teraphim, and also the Levite priest who had belonged to Micah. The people of the city did not expect anyone to attack them, so they were surprised by the attack of the Danites, and the surprise was greater than their ability to face it, so their resistance collapsed before the children of Dan, who took the city, burned it, and killed those in it.

18.26.1.en: Just as it is true to say that unpreparedness to defend the homeland against foreign invasion is the sure prelude to defeat before it, so also unpreparedness and spiritual heedlessness tempt the enemy of good to storm souls and gain control over them. Let us then always be watchful, knowing that our enemy is "a roaring lion, walking about, seeking whom he may devour," and let us prepare with prayers, reading the Holy Bible, repentance, and partaking of the Mysteries.

18.27.0.en: No one hastened to rescue them, not even the Sidonians, the inhabitants of Sidon, the original homeland of the people of Laish from which they had come. They did not rush to the aid of their brethren because of the distance of the city of Laish from the city of Sidon, and likewise the people of Laish had no alliances with any of the other neighboring peoples to cry to for help. The city of Laish, as the Scripture says, lay in the valley that is in Beth-rehob, a valley which is today in Lebanon, and in this valley there was a city called "Beth-rehob," from which the valley took its name. When the Danites took the city and settled in it, they rebuilt it anew after having burned it in their attack to take it.

18.28.0.en: They changed the name of the city from its old name "Laish" to a new name, "Dan," the name of their great forefather Dan, the son of Jacob by his wife Bilhah, Rachel's maid (Gen 30:6). Thus the tribe of Dan found a new land to take in its increase in numbers, so part of the tribe remained in their first portion in the southwest of the land of Canaan, and the other part lived in the city of "Laish" in the northeast.

18.29.0.en: Until the day of the captivity of the land: until the day when the Lord delivered them into the hands of the Philistines, who defeated them and took the ark of the covenant from them to their country, and the glory departed from Israel (1 Sam 4). The tribe set up Micah's graven image as a god for themselves, to worship and to perform rites for, and the people also consecrated the young Levite as priest for this god whom they worshipped. This was one of the signs of the people's spiritual decline and their departure from true worship in order to live according to their own desires.

18.30.0.en: Thus the Danites continued to worship the graven image, for which they appointed a priest who was not of the seed of Aaron, although the true house of God, the tabernacle of meeting, was still in "Shiloh," where lawful priests served in it. This shows the disunity among the tribes, their not gathering around the place of true worship, and their not submitting to the word of God and His Law.

18.30.1.en: The establishment of idol worship among the people of God in the age of the judges in the city of Dan perhaps encouraged Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who divided the kingdom after King Solomon and then set up images in Dan and in Bethel to turn them away from the worship of God that was in Jerusalem (1 Kgs 12:19-33). Although the Danites had possessed Laish and driven out the pagans from it, they returned and worshipped idols in the story of Micah. This is like many who begin with God and reject sin and then return to it of their own will a second time.
